26. The world of the act power of the functioning of Kudilai.
27. The world of the aid power of the functioning of Kudilai.
28. The world of the impelling power of the functioning of Kudilai.
29. The world of the substratum power of the dissolution of Kudilai.
30. The world of the instrument power of the dissolution of Kudilai.
31. The world of the season power of the dissolution of Kudilai.
32. The world of the act power of the dissolution of Kudilai.
33. The world of the aid power of the dissolution of Kudilai.
34. The world of the impelling power of the dissolution of Kudilai.
1. The world of pure maya.
2. The world of Kundali: know that these too are this Kudilai world.
commentary: Kudilai is pure maya in its first stirring as Om. It is the common ground in which the whole universe of word and meaning inheres. Its name means "the coiled one", and its own form is "many hoods", the image of the coiled serpent power. The two lines at the end say that the worlds of pure maya and of Kundali are this same Kudilai world under other names.

sections.title: The Tattva Worlds: Anava

tamil: 94. பசுத்துவ கரண அநாதி நித்திய ஆணவ சத்தி உலகு.
6. சகல கேவல விகற்பத்துவ ஆணவ குணசத்தி உலகு.
translation: 94. The world of the power of anava, beginningless and eternal, the instrument of the bound state.
1. The world of the form power of anava, as dense darkness.
2. The world of the own-form power of anava, effected through root ignorance.
3. The world of the nature power of anava, as the form of the states.
4. The world of the pervasion power of anava, non-dual with the three classes of souls.
5. The world of the pervading power of anava, in relation as the veiling of the Supreme and the soul.
6. The world of the quality power of anava, as the distinction of sakala and kevala.
7. The world of the particular power of anava, as predominance reaching as far as Nada.
8. The world of the colour power of anava.
9. The world of the being power of anava.
10. The world of the higher-order power of anava.
11. The world of the lower-order power of anava.
12. The world of the instrumental-cause power of anava.
13. The world of the particular instrumental-cause power of anava.
14. The world of the power of the arising of anava.
15. The world of the power of the functioning of anava.
16. The world of the power of the dissolution of anava.
17. The world of the substratum power of the arising of anava.
18. The world of the instrument power of the arising of anava.
19. The world of the season power of the arising of anava.
20. The world of the act power of the arising of anava.
21. The world of the aid power of the arising of anava.
22. The world of the impelling power of the arising of anava.
23. The world of the substratum power of the functioning of anava.
24. The world of the instrument power of the functioning of anava.
25. The world of the season power of the functioning of anava.
26. The world of the act power of the functioning of anava.
27. The world of the aid power of the functioning of anava.
28. The world of the impelling power of the functioning of anava.
29. The world of the substratum power of the dissolution of anava.
30. The world of the instrument power of the dissolution of anava.
31. The world of the season power of the dissolution of anava.
32. The world of the act power of the dissolution of anava.
33. The world of the aid power of the dissolution of anava.
34. The world of the impelling power of the dissolution of anava.
commentary: Anava, the soul's innate darkness, is given a full run of thirty-four powers like any tattva. It is beginningless and eternal; it is the instrument of the bound state. Its form is dense darkness, and its own form is root ignorance. It is one with all three classes of souls, and its reach extends as far as Nada. That even this darkness is named shows the reach of the word: nothing stands outside Ulagelam.

sections.title: The Tattva Worlds: Tirodhai

tamil: 95. கன்ம பக்குவ உபகார உத்தியோக அநாதிநித்திய திரோதை சத்தி உலகு.
2. ஞான அஞ்ஞான பாகியாந்தர வியாபாரத்துவ திரோதை சொரூபசத்தி உலகு.
7. கன்மானுபவ சுக வியாபார சாத்தியப் பிரேரக திரோதை விசேடசத்தி உலகு.
translation: 95. The world of the power of Tirodhai, beginningless and eternal, in its exertion to aid the ripening of karma.
1. The world of the form power of Tirodhai, as knowledge and ignorance.
2. The world of the own-form power of Tirodhai, as the outer and inner activity of knowledge and ignorance.
3. The world of the nature power of Tirodhai, as likeness to bondage.
4. The world of the pervasion power of Tirodhai, reaching as far as the supreme Bindu.
5. The world of the pervading power of Tirodhai, reaching as far as the supreme Nada.
6. The world of the quality power of Tirodhai, as impelling in keeping with karma.
7. The world of the particular power of Tirodhai, as impelling, effected through the activity of joy in the experience of karma.
8. The world of the colour power of Tirodhai.
9. The world of the being power of Tirodhai.
10. The world of the higher-order power of Tirodhai.
11. The world of the lower-order power of Tirodhai.
12. The world of the instrumental-cause power of Tirodhai.
13. The world of the particular instrumental-cause power of Tirodhai.
14. The world of the power of the arising of Tirodhai.
15. The world of the power of the functioning of Tirodhai.
16. The world of the power of the dissolution of Tirodhai.
17. The world of the substratum power of the arising of Tirodhai.
18. The world of the instrument power of the arising of Tirodhai.
19. The world of the season power of the arising of Tirodhai.
20. The world of the act power of the arising of Tirodhai.
21. The world of the aid power of the arising of Tirodhai.
22. The world of the impelling power of the arising of Tirodhai.
23. The world of the substratum power of the functioning of Tirodhai.
24. The world of the instrument power of the functioning of Tirodhai.
25. The world of the season power of the functioning of Tirodhai.
26. The world of the act power of the functioning of Tirodhai.
27. The world of the aid power of the functioning of Tirodhai.
28. The world of the impelling power of the functioning of Tirodhai.
29. The world of the substratum power of the dissolution of Tirodhai.
30. The world of the instrument power of the dissolution of Tirodhai.
31. The world of the season power of the dissolution of Tirodhai.
32. The world of the act power of the dissolution of Tirodhai.
33. The world of the aid power of the dissolution of Tirodhai.
34. The world of the impelling power of the dissolution of Tirodhai.
commentary: Tirodhai is the veiling power: the Lord's beginningless, eternal Power, which keeps the soul's knowledge veiled while its karma ripens. It is "like bondage" in nature, yet it works to aid the ripening of karma, and its reach extends as far as the supreme Bindu and the supreme Nada. Its veiling is His care for the soul, not opposition to it. Its run has the full thirty-four worlds.

sections.title: The Tattva Worlds: The Soul's Power of Consciousness

tamil: 1. இச்சா ஞானக் கிரியா சமவாயத்துவ ஆன்மரூபசத்தி உலகு.
5. அஷ்டசித்தி யனுபவ சாத்திய ஆன்மவியாபக சத்தி உலகு.
translation: 96. The world of the soul's power of consciousness, beginningless and eternal.
1. The world of the form power of the soul, as the inherence of desire, knowledge and action.
2. The world of the own-form power of the soul, as the sense of "I" and the sense of "mine".
3. The world of the nature power of the soul, as relation reaching as far as the tattvas.
4. The world of the pervasion power of the soul, reaching as far as the tattvic.
5. The world of the pervading power of the soul, effected through the experience of the eight attainments (siddhis).
6. The world of the quality power of the soul, as dependent knowledge.
7. The world of the particular power of the soul, as relation to what is beyond the tattvas.
8. The world of the colour power of the soul.
9. The world of the being power of the soul.
10. The world of the higher-order power of the soul.
11. The world of the lower-order power of the soul.
12. The world of the instrumental-cause power of the soul.
13. The world of the particular instrumental-cause power of the soul.
14. The world of the power of the functioning of the soul.
15. The world of the substratum power of the functioning of the soul.
16. The world of the instrument power of the functioning of the soul.
17. The world of the season power of the functioning of the soul.
18. The world of the act power of the functioning of the soul.
19. The world of the aid power of the functioning of the soul.
20. The world of the impelling power of the functioning of the soul.
commentary: Head 96 is the soul's own power of consciousness (ciṟcatti), beginningless and eternal. From here to head 101 the runs give only the functioning phase: these powers never arise and never dissolve, so they have no worlds of arising or dissolution. The soul holds desire, knowledge and action together; it can bind itself to "I" and "mine" and reach out through every tattva, yet it also stands in relation to what is beyond the tattvas.

sections.title: The Tattva Worlds: The Power of Desire

tamil: 97. சர்வ இச்சாகாரண சமவாய அநாதிநித்திய இச்சாசத்தி உலகு.
6. சிவ சையோகசம்பந்த வாசாபிரேரகத்துவ இச்சை குண சத்தி உலகு.
translation: 97. The world of the power of desire, beginningless and eternal, inhering as the cause of all desire.
1. The world of the form power of desire, as the instrumental cause that is the basis.
2. The world of the own-form power of desire, as effected through the form power of all things.
3. The world of the nature power of desire, as grace to souls.
4. The world of the pervasion power of desire, reaching as far as Tirodhai.
5. The world of the pervading power of desire, as the true Guru, whose form is knowledge, appearing with form.
6. The world of the quality power of desire, as what impels speech, in relation of conjunction with Siva.
7. The world of the particular power of desire, in relation of conjunction with what has form and what is formless.
8. The world of the colour power of desire.
9. The world of the being power of desire.
10. The world of the higher-order power of desire.
11. The world of the lower-order power of desire.
12. The world of the instrumental-cause power of desire.
13. The world of the particular instrumental-cause power of desire.
14. The world of the power of the functioning of desire.
15. The world of the substratum power of the functioning of desire.
16. The world of the instrument power of the functioning of desire.
17. The world of the season power of the functioning of desire.
18. The world of the act power of the functioning of desire.
19. The world of the aid power of the functioning of desire.
20. The world of the impelling power of the functioning of desire.
commentary: With head 97 the catalogue reaches the Lord's own Powers. Desire (iccai) here is God's will, the cause of all desire. Its nature is grace to souls; it reaches as far as Tirodhai, and it comes to souls as the true Guru, whose form is knowledge, appearing in a form they can meet.

sections.title: The Tattva Worlds: The Power of Knowledge

tamil: 4. ஆன்ம விவித குண வியாபாரத்துவ ஞானவியாபகசத்தி உலகு.
translation: 98. The world of the power of knowledge, beginningless and eternal, inhering as the cause of all knowledge.
1. The world of the own-form power of knowledge, in the form of all souls.
2. The world of the nature power of knowledge, as what impels all souls.
3. The world of the pervasion power of knowledge, over desire alone.
4. The world of the pervading power of knowledge, as activity in the various qualities of souls.
5. The world of the quality power of knowledge, as beyond direct perception.
6. The world of the particular power of knowledge, as the separation of the bound soul from bondage.
7. The world of the colour power of knowledge.
8. The world of the being power of knowledge.
9. The world of the instrumental-cause power of knowledge.
10. The world of the particular instrumental-cause power of knowledge.
11. The world of the higher-order power of knowledge.
12. The world of the lower-order power of knowledge.
13. The world of the power of the functioning of knowledge.
14. The world of the substratum power of the functioning of knowledge.
15. The world of the instrument power of the functioning of knowledge.
16. The world of the season power of the functioning of knowledge.
17. The world of the act power of the functioning of knowledge.
18. The world of the aid power of the functioning of knowledge.
19. The world of the impelling power of the functioning of knowledge.
commentary: The Lord's power of knowledge takes the form of all souls and moves them, yet no sense perceives it. Its particular work is to part the bound soul from its bondage. The run has nineteen items: it has no separate form item, and it lists the instrumental causes before the higher and lower order, as printed.

sections.title: The Tattva Worlds: The Power of Action

tamil: 99. சர்வ கிரியாகாரணசமவாய அநாதிநித்திய கிரியா சத்தி உலகு.
1. தூல சூக்குமப் பிரபஞ்ச சமவாய அசமவாய சர்வ கரணக் கிரியாரூபசத்தி உலகு.
2. சீவ கன்ம வியக்திப் பிரேரக கிரியாசொரூபசத்தி உலகு.
4. தூல சூக்கும சரீரமாத்திர கிரியா வியாத்திசத்தி உலகு.
translation: 99. The world of the power of action, beginningless and eternal, inhering as the cause of all action.
1. The world of the form power of action, as every instrument, in inherence and non-inherence, of the gross and subtle universe.
2. The world of the own-form power of action, which impels the manifestation of the karma of individual souls.
3. The world of the nature power of action, as exertion in the five functions.
4. The world of the pervasion power of action, over the gross and subtle bodies alone.
5. The world of the pervading power of action, effected through many forms.
6. The world of the quality power of action, as what impels the three gunas.
7. The world of the particular power of action, as exertion in the means.
8. The world of the colour power of action.
9. The world of the being power of action.
10. The world of the higher-order power of action.
11. The world of the lower-order power of action.
12. The world of the instrumental-cause power of action.
13. The world of the particular instrumental-cause power of action.
14. The world of the power of the functioning of action.
15. The world of the substratum power of the functioning of action.
16. The world of the instrument power of the functioning of action.
17. The world of the season power of the functioning of action.
18. The world of the act power of the functioning of action.
19. The world of the aid power of the functioning of action.
20. The world of the impelling power of the functioning of action.
commentary: The power of action is the instrument of the whole universe, gross and subtle. It brings each soul's karma into manifestation, labours in the five functions (creation, protection, withdrawal, veiling and grace) and moves the three gunas. Even the soul's exertion in its spiritual means is this Power at work.

sections.title: The Tattva Worlds: The Power of Consciousness

tamil: 1. காரண காரிய அதீதப் பிரகாசத்துவ சித்ரூபசத்தி உலகு.
2. பாகி யாந்தர அதீத ஞான சாத்திய சிற்சொரூபசத்தி உலகு.
translation: 100. The world of the power of consciousness, beginningless and eternal, the experience in which supreme joy begins.
1. The world of the form power of consciousness, as light beyond cause and effect.
2. The world of the own-form power of consciousness, effected through the knowledge beyond outer and inner.
3. The world of the nature power of consciousness, as self-luminosity.
4. The world of the pervasion power of consciousness, reaching as far as the supreme Bindu.
5. The world of the pervading power of consciousness, reaching as far as the supreme Siva.
6. The world of the quality power of consciousness, as the gateway to the experience of bliss.
7. The world of the particular power of consciousness, discerning the truth.
8. The world of the colour power of consciousness.
9. The world of the being power of consciousness.
10. The world of the higher-order power of consciousness.
11. The world of the lower-order power of consciousness.
12. The world of the instrumental-cause power of consciousness.
13. The world of the particular instrumental-cause power of consciousness.
14. The world of the power of the functioning of consciousness.
15. The world of the substratum power of the functioning of consciousness.
16. The world of the instrument power of the functioning of consciousness.
17. The world of the season power of the functioning of consciousness.
18. The world of the act power of the functioning of consciousness.
19. The world of the aid power of the functioning of consciousness.
20. The world of the impelling power of the functioning of consciousness.
commentary: Head 100 is consciousness itself (cit), where supreme joy begins to be tasted. It is light beyond cause and effect, shining by itself, reaching as far as the supreme Siva, and it is the gateway to the experience of bliss. This is the light toward which Vallalar's whole path rises.

sections.title: The Tattva Worlds: The Supreme Power

tamil: 101. அநாதி நித்தியத்துவ பரானுபவ ஆதார பராசத்தி உலகு.
1. ஆதியந்த பூரண வியக்தி சாத்தியத்துவ பரைரூபசத்தி உலகு.
translation: 101. The world of the supreme Power, as beginningless and eternal, the support of the supreme experience.
1. The world of the form power of Parai (the supreme Power), effected through full manifestation from beginning to end.
2. The world of the own-form power of Parai, effected through inherence in the light of consciousness.
3. The world of the nature power of Parai, as aid to the own form of Siva.
4. The world of the pervasion power of Parai, reaching as far as Siva.
5. The world of the pervading power of Parai, the cause of the five forms.
6. The world of the particular power of Parai, the notion of Siva's grace.
7. The world of the colour power of Parai.
8. The world of the being power of Parai.
9. The world of the higher-order power of Parai.
10. The world of the lower-order power of Parai.
11. The world of the instrumental-cause power of Parai.
12. The world of the particular instrumental-cause power of Parai.
13. The world of the power of the functioning of Parai.
14. The world of the substratum power of the functioning of Parai.
15. The world of the instrument power of the functioning of Parai.
16. The world of the season power of the functioning of Parai.
17. The world of the act power of the functioning of Parai.
18. The world of the aid power of the functioning of Parai.
19. The world of the impelling power of the functioning of Parai.
commentary: Head 101 is Parai, the supreme Power, the support of the supreme experience. Her form is full manifestation from beginning to end; she is one with the light of consciousness, she serves Siva's own form, and her particular power is Siva's intent (caṅkaṟpam) to give grace. Through this Power of Grace the soul is brought to Him.

sections.title: The Tattva Worlds: The Supreme Siva and the Supreme Nada

tamil: 1. இச்சா ஞான சாத்திய பரநாத சொரூபசத்தி உலகு.
2. காரணக் கிரியா வியாபாரத்துவ பரநாத சுபாவசத்தி உலகு.
4. பூதாதி நாதபரியந்த பூரணத்துவ பரநாத வியாபகசத்தி உலகு.
translation: 102. The world of the supreme Siva, which impels aid to the experience of Brahman (the Absolute).
103. The world of the form power of the supreme Nada, of supreme bliss.
1. The world of the own-form power of the supreme Nada, effected through desire and knowledge.
2. The world of the nature power of the supreme Nada, as the activity of causal action.
3. The world of the pervasion power of the supreme Nada, to the very end of the six modes of being.
4. The world of the pervading power of the supreme Nada, as fullness from the elements and the rest as far as Nada.
5. The world of the quality power of the supreme Nada, as knowledge of all.
6. The world of the particular power of the supreme Nada, effected without basis.
7. The world of the colour power of the supreme Nada.
8. The world of the being power of the supreme Nada.
These are the tattva worlds.
commentary: The tattva worlds end at the summit: the supreme Siva, who impels aid toward the experience of the Absolute, and the supreme Nada, of supreme bliss, with eight powers. The "six modes of being" (ṣaṭpāvam) are the six changes of all that exists: birth, existence, growth, change, decline and death. With the closing line, Group 1 is complete: 103 tattva worlds, from the elements to the supreme Nada, all within the one word Ulagelam.

sections.title: The Tattvic Worlds: The Worlds of Brahma and Indra

translation: (2. The tattvic worlds)
Now the tattvic worlds:
1. The world of Brahma in the creation of the elements.
2. The world of Brahma that takes the instruments for the self.
3. The world of Brahma in the creation of the physical.
4. The world of Brahma that takes the tanmatras (the subtle elements) for the self.
5. The world of Brahma that takes prakriti (primal matter) for the self.
6. The world of Brahma of the limb.
7. The world of Brahma of the sub-limb.
8. The world of Brahma of the minor limb.
9. The world of the root Brahma.
1. The world of Indra of the organs of knowledge.
2. The world of Indra of the organs of action.
3. The world of Indra of the three cravings (eshanas).
4. The world of Indra of the limb.
5. The world of Indra of the sub-limb.
6. The world of Indra of the minor limb.
1. The world of the Prajapatya (of Prajapati) liberation that is the experience of the pure instruments.
2. The world of the Prajapatya liberation that is the experience of the Gayatri.
3. The world of the Prajapatya liberation of I-ness.
4. The world of the Prajapatya liberation of the contemplation "I am He" (soham).
5. The world of the Prajapatya liberation of oneness with prakriti.
1. The world of the Aindra (of Indra) liberation that is the experience of the enjoyment of prakriti.
2. The world of the Aindra liberation that is the experience of the senses' direct perception.
commentary: Group 2 is the tattvic worlds: worlds that derive from the tattvas and stay within them. Here stand the worlds of Brahma, the creator, and of Indra, king of the gods, and the liberations of Prajapati's and Indra's realms: the experience of the pure instruments, of the Gayatri (the Vedic prayer to the sun), of I-ness, of "I am He", of oneness with prakriti, of the senses. The three cravings are for children, wealth and the world's regard. Vallalar names all of them liberations, and places all of them within the tattvas.

sections.title: The Tattvic Worlds: The Liberations of the Mind, Body and Elements

translation: 1. The world of the liberation that is the experience of the mind's direct perception.
2. The world of the liberation that takes the mind for the self.
1. The world of the liberation of the intellect tattva.
2. The world of the liberation that takes the intellect for the self.
1. The world of the liberation of the sense of "I".
2. The world of the liberation that takes the sense of "I" for the self.
1. The world of the liberation of cittam (the reflecting mind).
2. The world of the liberation that takes cittam for the self.
1. The world of the liberation of prakriti (primal matter).
2. The world of the liberation that takes prakriti for the self.
1. The world of the liberation of objects that takes the body for the self.
2. The world of the liberation that takes the non-self.
1. The world of the liberation of the elements.
2. The world of the liberation that takes the elements for the self.
1. The world of the liberation of nectar.
2. The world of the liberation of herbs.
3. The world of the liberation of the tanmatras (the subtle elements).
1. The world of the liberation of the senses.
2. The world of the liberation that takes the senses for the self.
commentary: Most pairs give the liberation of a tattva and the liberation that takes that tattva for the self: mind, intellect, the sense of "I", cittam, prakriti, the elements, the senses. Taking the body, or the non-self, for the self belongs here too, and so do the liberations sought through nectar and herbs. Each is still a world within the tattvas.

sections.title: The Tattvic Worlds: The Worlds of Vishnu and the Liberations by Destruction

tamil: 1. தசபதார்த்த கன்மநாச நிஷ்கிரியாலக்ஷிய குணான்மிய விகற்ப முத்தி உலகு.
2. பாவ புண்ணிய பிராரத்தகன்மநாச லக்ஷிய ஜீவான்மிய அணுவாதீத முத்தி உலகு.
4. பிரகிருதிநாச மோகினி காரியான்மிய விகற்ப முத்தி உலகு.
translation: 1. The world of the liberation that aims at the destruction of the aggregates (skandhas).
2. The world of the liberation that aims at the destruction of the elements.
3. The world of the liberation that aims at the destruction of the body.
4. The world of the liberation that aims at the destruction of karma.
5. The world of the liberation that aims at the destruction of the qualities.
6. The world of the liberation that aims at the destruction of the instruments.
7. The world of the liberation that aims at the destruction of prakriti (primal matter).
1. The world of Vishnu that takes time for the self.
2. The world of the liberation of time.
1. The world of the liberation that takes niyati (order) for the self.
2. The world of the liberation of niyati.
1. The world of Vishnu that takes kalā for the self.
2. The world of the liberation that takes kalā for the self.
1. The world of Vishnu that takes vidya (limited knowledge) for the self.
2. The world of the liberation of vidya.
1. The world of Vishnu that takes raga (attachment) for the self.
2. The world of the liberation of raga.
1. The world of Vishnu that takes purusha (the soul as experiencer) for the self.
2. The world of the liberation of purusha.
1. The world of Vishnu that takes maya for the self.
2. The world of the liberation of maya.
1. The world of the liberation of distinction that takes the qualities for the self, aiming at actionlessness through the destruction of karma in the ten categories.
2. The world of the liberation beyond the atom, which takes the individual soul for the self, aiming at the destruction of sin and merit and of prarabdha karma (the karma already bearing fruit).
3. The world of the liberation that takes the individual soul for the self, aiming at the destruction of the elements.
4. The world of the liberation of distinction by the destruction of prakriti, which takes the effect of mohini for the self.
5. The world of the liberation by the destruction of time.
6. The world of the liberation by the destruction of niyati.
7. The world of the liberation by the destruction of kalā.
8. The world of the liberation by the destruction of vidya.
9. The world of the liberation by the destruction of raga.
10. The world of the liberation by the destruction of purusha.
11. The world of the liberation by the destruction of maya.
1. The world of Vishnu of the limb.
2. The world of Vishnu of the sub-limb.
3. The world of Vishnu of the minor limb.
4. The world of the root Vishnu.
commentary: These liberations seek the destruction of something: the aggregates (the five constituents of the person in Buddhist teaching), the elements, the body, karma, the qualities, prakriti, and the limiting tattvas from time to maya. Between them stand the worlds of Vishnu that take a tattva for the self. Whether a path identifies with a tattva or labours to destroy it, its goal stays a tattvic world. Prarabdha is the karma already bearing fruit in this life.

sections.title: The Tattvic Worlds: The Liberations Held by the Schools

tamil: 1. நிகம நித்திய வாதித கர்மசாத்தியானுபவ முத்தி உலகு.
3. தர்க்க நிச்சய வாதித அணுவிபாகப் பரமாணுத்துவ அனுபவ முத்தி உலகு.
4. சத்த நித்திய பரிணாம சாத்தியானுபவ முத்தி உலகு.
6. சௌபாதிக சின்மாத்திர வாதித பிரகாச சாத்திய முத்தி உலகு.
7. பிரகிருதி புருட வாதித சாங்கியானுப முத்தி உலகு.
8. நியதி ஏகத்துவ அனுபவ விகற்ப முத்தி உலகு.
11. பக்தசேவாலக்ஷிய வாதித ஏகதேச மோகினி விகற்ப முத்தி உலகு.
12. நாமாக்ஷரலக்ஷிய வாதித ஏகதேச விகற்ப மோகினி முத்தி உலகு.
translation: 1. The world of the liberation that is experience effected through karma, held by those who argue that the Veda is eternal.
2. The world of the liberation that is the experience of inertness, through the destruction of karma before and after.
3. The world of the liberation that is the experience of ultimate atomicity in the separation of atoms, held by those who argue from the certainty of logic.
4. The world of the liberation that is experience effected through the transformation of eternal sound.
5. The world of the liberation that is indirect experience, held by those who argue for inquiry.
6. The world of the liberation effected through light, held by those who argue for consciousness alone, with adjuncts.
7. The world of the liberation of Sankhya experience, held by those who argue for prakriti and purusha.
8. The world of the liberation of distinction that is the experience of the oneness of niyati.
9. The world of the liberation whose aim is the maker of maya.
10. The world of the liberation of partial distinction whose aim is the maker of maya.
11. The world of the liberation of partial distinction in mohini, held by those who argue for the devotee's service as the aim.
12. The world of the mohini liberation of partial distinction, held by those who argue for the letters of the Name as the aim.
13. The world of the partial liberation in maya, held by those who argue for the indescribable.
14. The world of the liberation held by those who argue that the soul is Brahman (the Absolute).
15. The world of the liberation held by those who argue for duality, with distinction and karma.
16. The world of the liberation held by those who argue for non-duality through the contemplation "I am He" (soham).
commentary: Here the liberations are named by the doctrines that hold them: the eternal Veda and its rites, logic and its ultimate atoms, eternal sound, inquiry, consciousness alone, the prakriti and purusha of Sankhya, niyati, the maker of maya, the devotee's service, the letters of the divine Name, the indescribable, "the soul is Brahman", dualism, and the non-dualism of "I am He". Vallalar counts each of them as a tattvic world: an attainment that stays within the tattvas.

sections.title: The Tattvic Worlds: The Liberations by Planets, Elixir, Mantra and the Gods

translation: 1. The world of the liberation by the planets.
2. The world of the liberation by kalpa (elixir).
3. The world of the liberation by mantra.
4. The world of the liberation by yantra.
5. The world of the liberation by the sun.
6. The world of the liberation by fire.
7. The world of the liberation by the gods of many distinctions.
commentary: The tattvic worlds close with the liberations sought through the planets, the elixirs (kaṟpam) of the Tamil siddha tradition, mantra (sacred formula), yantra (sacred diagram), the sun, fire, and the gods in their many distinctions.

sections.title: The Liberation Worlds of the Primal, Eternal Impellers: Rudra to Nada

translation: (3. The liberation worlds of the primal, eternal impellers)
Now the liberation worlds of the primal, eternal impellers:
1. The world of Rudra.
2. The world of Pranava-Rudra.
3. The world of Upa-Rudra.
4. The world of Pratyanga-Rudra.
1. The world of Mahesvara.
2. The world of Pranava-Mahesvara.
3. The world of Upa-Mahesvara.
4. The world of Pratyanga-Mahesvara.
1. The world of Sadasiva.
2. The world of Pranava-Sadasiva.
3. The world of Upa-Sadasiva.
4. The world of Pratyanga-Sadasiva.
1. The world of Bindu.
2. The world of Pranava-Bindu.
3. The world of Upa-Bindu.
4. The world of Pratyanga-Bindu.
1. The world of Nada.
2. The world of Pranava-Nada.
3. The world of Upa-Nada.
4. The world of Pratyanga-Nada.
commentary: Group 3 is the liberation worlds of the primal, eternal impellers: the lords Rudra, Mahesvara, Sadasiva, Bindu and Nada, who set maya and souls to work. They stand above the tattvic worlds, in the Lord's own order. Each lord has four worlds: his own, and those of Pranava- (of Om), Upa- (subsidiary) and Pratyanga- (of the minor limb).

sections.title: The Liberation Worlds of the Primal, Eternal Impellers: Nada in the Five Functions

tamil: 1. பிரகாச விபாக அந்தகார சையோகப் பிரேரக நாத சுத்த உலகு.
2. சத்தி விபாக அசத்திய சையோகப் பிரேரக நாத சுத்த உலகு.
3. கலாதி பந்தப் பிரேரக நாத சுத்த உலகு.
4. தத்துவக்கியான விபாகப் பிரேரக நாத சுத்த உலகு.
5. விஷயசுக இச்சாப் பிரேரக நாத சுத்த உலகு.
translation: 1. The world of Nada in the creation of all powers.
2. The world of Nada in the creation of all bondage.
3. The world of Nada in the creation of all individual souls.
4. The world of Nada in the creation of all mantras.
5. The world of Nada in eternal creation.
1. The world of Nada in the protection of all powers.
2. The world of Nada in the protection of all bondage.
3. The world of Nada in the protection of all individual souls.
4. The world of Nada in the protection of all mantras.
5. The world of Nada in eternal protection.
1. The world of Nada in the withdrawal of all powers.
2. The world of Nada in the withdrawal of all bondage.
3. The world of Nada in the withdrawal of all individual souls.
4. The world of Nada in the withdrawal of all mantras.
5. The world of Nada in eternal withdrawal.
1. The pure world of Nada, which impels separation from light and conjunction with darkness.
2. The pure world of Nada, which impels separation from power and conjunction with untruth.
3. The pure world of Nada, which impels the bond of kalā and the rest.
4. The pure world of Nada, which impels separation from the knowledge of the tattvas.
5. The pure world of Nada, which impels desire for the joy of objects.
1. The world of Nada in inner grace.
2. The world of Nada in outer grace.
3. The world of Nada in grace in the prakti form.
4. The world of Nada in the grace of notion.
5. The world of Nada in the grace of mantra.
commentary: Nada carries out the Lord's five functions: creation, protection and withdrawal of all powers, bonds, souls and mantras; the fourth, veiling, in which Nada impels the soul toward bondage; and grace. Even the veiling worlds are called pure, for the bond serves the soul's ripening and grace follows it. Grace comes inwardly, outwardly, through a form, through His intent and through mantra. Prakti (225.3) is so printed in every edition, and the word is uncertain; it may stand for vyakti, "manifest".

sections.title: The Liberation Worlds of the Primal, Eternal Impellers: The Lords of the Pranava

tamil: 1. அசுத்த போக போக்கியப் பிரேரக நிமித்த சுத்தவித்தைப் பிரத்தியாங்க அதிகரண சுத்தமாயா ஸ்தூலப்பிரணவருத்திர உலகு.

3. சுத்தபோக போக்கியப் பிரேரக நிமித்த சுத்தவித்தை சாங்காதிகரண சுத்தமாயா ஸ்தூலப்பிரணவாணு ருத்திர உலகு.
1. நிமித்தப் பிரேரக நிமித்த மயேசுரப் பிரத்தியாங்க அதிகரண சுத்தமாயா மகாஸ்தூலப்பிரணவாணு ஈசுர உலகு.
2. நிமித்தப் பிரேரக நிமித்த மயேசுர உபாங்க அதிகரண சுத்த மாயா மகாஸ்தூலப்பிரணவாணு ஈசுர உலகு.
1. நிமித்த சாதாக்கியப் பிரத்தியாங்க அதிகரண சுத்தமாயா சூக்குமப்பிரணவாணு சதாசிவ உலகு.
2. மஹா ஸ்தூலப் பிரேரக நிமித்த சாதாக்கிய உபாங்க அதிகரண சுத்தமாயா சூக்குமப் பிரணவ சதாசிவ உலகு.
3. மஹா ஸ்தூலப் பிரேரக நிமித்த சாதாக்கிய சாங்காதிகரண சுத்தமாயா சூக்குமப் பிரணவாணு சதாசிவ உலகு.
1. சூக்குமப் பிரேரக நிமித்த விந்துப் பிரத்தியாங்க அதிகரண சுத்தமாயா மஹாசூக்குமப் பிரணவாணுச் சத்தி உலகு.
2. சூக்குமப் பிரேரக நிமித்த விந்து உபாங்க அதிகரண சுத்தமாயா மஹாசூக்குமப் பிரணவாணுச் சத்தி உலகு.
3. சூக்குமப் பிரேரக நிமித்த விந்து சாங்காதிகரண சுத்தமாயா மஹாசூக்குமப் பிரணவாணுச் சத்தி உலகு.
1. மஹாசூக்குமப் பிரேரக நிமித்த நாதப் பிரத்தியாங்க அதிகரண சுத்தமாயா காரணப் பிரணவாணுச் சிவ உலகு.
2. மகாசூக்குமப் பிரேரக நிமித்த நாத உபாங்க அதிகரண சுத்த மாயா காரணப் பிரணவாணுச் சிவ உலகு.
3. மகாசூக்குமப் பிரேரக நிமித்த சாங்காதிகரண சுத்தமாயா காரணப் பிரணவாணுச் சிவ உலகு.
translation: 1. The world of Rudra of the gross pranava (Om) in pure maya, whose substratum is the minor limb of pure vidya, as the instrumental cause that impels impure enjoyment and the enjoyed.
2. The world of Rudra of the gross pranava in pure maya, whose substratum is the sub-limb of pure vidya, as the instrumental cause that impels pure-impure enjoyment and the enjoyed.
3. The world of Rudra of the gross pranava-atom in pure maya, whose substratum is pure vidya complete with limbs, as the instrumental cause that impels pure enjoyment and the enjoyed.
1. The world of Isvara of the great gross pranava-atom in pure maya, whose substratum is the minor limb of Mahesvara, as the instrumental cause that impels the instrumental cause.
2. The world of Isvara of the great gross pranava-atom in pure maya, whose substratum is the sub-limb of Mahesvara, as the instrumental cause that impels the instrumental cause.
1. The world of Sadasiva of the subtle pranava-atom in pure maya, whose substratum is the minor limb of Sadakhya, as the instrumental cause.
2. The world of Sadasiva of the subtle pranava in pure maya, whose substratum is the sub-limb of Sadakhya, as the instrumental cause that impels the great gross.
3. The world of Sadasiva of the subtle pranava-atom in pure maya, whose substratum is Sadakhya complete with limbs, as the instrumental cause that impels the great gross.
1. The world of Shakti of the great subtle pranava-atom in pure maya, whose substratum is the minor limb of Bindu, as the instrumental cause that impels the subtle.
2. The world of Shakti of the great subtle pranava-atom in pure maya, whose substratum is the sub-limb of Bindu, as the instrumental cause that impels the subtle.
3. The world of Shakti of the great subtle pranava-atom in pure maya, whose substratum is Bindu complete with limbs, as the instrumental cause that impels the subtle.
1. The world of Siva of the causal pranava-atom in pure maya, whose substratum is the minor limb of Nada, as the instrumental cause that impels the great subtle.
2. The world of Siva of the causal pranava-atom in pure maya, whose substratum is the sub-limb of Nada, as the instrumental cause that impels the great subtle.
3. The world of Siva of the causal pranava-atom in pure maya, whose substratum is complete with limbs, as the instrumental cause that impels the great subtle.
commentary: Rudra, Isvara, Sadasiva, Shakti and Siva appear as lords of the pranava, Om, in pure maya, in five grades: gross, great gross, subtle, great subtle and causal. Each rests on a limb of a pure tattva (pure vidya, Mahesvara, Sadakhya, Bindu, Nada) and acts as the instrumental cause that impels the grade below. Where the print leaves a word out (228.1, 230.3), the translation does the same.

translation: 1. The world of the power of desire in conjunction with prakriti (primal matter), the cause of the impure, pure-impure and pure desire of the three classes of souls.
2. The world of the power of desire in conjunction with mohini (the deluding maya).
3. The world of the power of desire in conjunction with Bindu.
1. The world of the power of knowledge in conjunction with prakriti, the cause of the impure and pure-impure knowledge of the three classes of souls.
2. The world of the power of knowledge in conjunction with mohini.
3. The world of the power of knowledge in conjunction with Bindu.
1. The world of the power of action in conjunction with prakriti, of the three classes of souls, impure and pure-impure.
2. The world of the power of action in conjunction with mohini.
3. The world of the power of action in conjunction with Bindu.
1. The world of the primal Power in conjunction with prakriti, the cause of the impure, pure-impure and pure love of joy of the three classes of souls.
2. The world of the primal Power in conjunction with mohini.
3. The world of the primal Power in conjunction with Bindu.
1. The world of Parai (the supreme Power) in conjunction with prakriti, the cause of the impure, pure-impure and pure experience of the three classes of souls.
2. The world of Parai in conjunction with mohini.
3. The world of Parai in conjunction with Bindu.
commentary: The Lord's five Powers, desire, knowledge, action, the primal Power and Parai, each work in conjunction (caiyōkam) with prakriti, with mohini and with Bindu. Joined with prakriti, they cause the desire, knowledge, love of joy and experience of the three classes of souls in their impure, pure-impure and pure states.

3. சுத்த கரண சூக்கும வேக சங்கற்பப் பிரத்தியக்ஷ லக்ஷியானுபவ யோகயோகமுத்தி உலகு.
1. நாதோற்பவ சுத்த நிஷ்கள சாமானிய விந்து வேதன ஸ்தூலப் பிரத்தியக்ஷ லக்ஷியானுபவ ஞானச்சரியாமுத்தி உலகு.

4. சூக்கும விசேடப் பிரத்தியக்ஷ லக்ஷிய ஞானஞானமுத்தி உலகு.
translation: (4. The worlds of means and attainment in the pure tattvas)
Now the worlds of means and attainment in the pure tattvas:
1. The world of the liberation of charya-charya, the experience whose aim is the general, gross act, in the distinctions of the pure divine form arising from Bindu.
2. The world of the liberation of charya-kriya, the experience whose aim is the particular of the general, gross act, in the distinctions of the pure divine form arising from Bindu.
3. The world of the liberation of charya-yoga, the experience whose aim is the mental, general, gross notion, in the distinctions of the pure divine form arising from Bindu.
4. The world of the liberation of charya-jnana, the experience whose aim is the particular of the mental, general, gross notion, in the distinctions of the pure divine form arising from Bindu.
1. The world of the liberation of kriya-charya, the experience whose aim is the general, gross act of worship, with distinctions, toward the divine form on the pure seat arising from Bindu.

2. The world of the liberation of kriya-kriya, the experience whose aim is the particular of the general, gross act of worship, with distinctions, toward the divine form on the pure seat arising from Bindu.
3. The world of the liberation of kriya-yoga, the experience whose aim is the gross notion of mental worship.
4. The world of the liberation of kriya-jnana, the experience whose aim is the particular of the gross notion of mental worship.
1. The world of the liberation of yoga-charya, the experience whose aim is the direct perception, in subtle notion through the pure instruments, of what is pure, general, with form and formless.
2. The world of the liberation of yoga-kriya, the experience whose aim is particular direct perception.
3. The world of the liberation of yoga-yoga, the experience whose aim is the direct perception, in subtle, swift notion, through the pure instruments.
4. The world of the liberation of yoga-jnana, the experience whose aim is particular direct perception.
1. The world of the liberation of jnana-charya, the experience whose aim is the gross direct perception, in awareness, of Bindu, pure, formless and general, arising from Nada.
2. The world of the liberation of jnana-kriya, the experience whose aim is the particular of gross direct perception.
3. The world of the liberation of jnana-yoga, whose aim is subtle direct perception.
4. The world of the liberation of jnana-jnana, whose aim is subtle, particular direct perception.
commentary: The fourth group holds the worlds reached by practice: the means (cātaṉa) and what they attain (cāttiya), within the pure tattvas, the pure order that lies above maya's impure worlds. It opens with the sixteen stages of the four ways as liberations. In charya the aim is the outward act of service before the divine form (mūrtti) that arises from Bindu. In kriya it is worship, first outward, then in the mind. In yoga it is direct perception through the pure instruments. In jnana it is the direct perception of Bindu itself, formless and arising from Nada. Each step turns further inward.

commentary: Breath control gathers the breath: its first three parts are purifying rites (Skt. utplavana, aghamarṣaṇa, mārjana), then come the movement of the root fire and the ascent; the ten nadis (channels of the breath) become one, and the breath is let out, drawn in and held, up to Nada, the pranava (Om) and ajapa, the prayer the breath repeats of itself. Withdrawal rests on discernment, faith and dispassion. Concentration and meditation take their supports from the centres of the body, from mantra, word and letter, and from God with form and formless, up to the Light (cōti).

Nirosata and the naṭa centres are left as printed, since their sense is uncertain. The attainments (siddhis), becoming minute, vast, heavy or light, are also yoga worlds; Vallalar simply counts them here.

sections.title: The Worlds of Means and Attainment: The Saiva Liberations

tamil: 1. சகள நிஷ்கள சையோக சம்பவ சகளாகள சாதாக்கிய பஞ்சகாக்கிரகண்ணிய சதாசிவான்ம பாவ பாகியார்ச்சித ஸ்தூல கிரியாலக்ஷிய ஆகம சுத்தசைவ முத்தி உலகு.
2. சகள நிஷ்கள சையோக சம்பவ சகளாகள சாதாக்கிய பஞ்சகாக்கிரகண்ணிய சதாசிவான்ம பாவ அந்தரார்ச்சித சங்கற்ப கிரியாலக்ஷிய கிரியாஞான சுத்தசைவமுத்தி உலகு.

16. சர்வபேதசவிகற்ப சத்தி சாமானியோற்பவ பரிக்கிரகப் பிரகாச பூரணாயிக்கிய லக்ஷிய வாமசித்தாந்த முத்தி உலகு.

18. சிவவிரதத்துவார வயிந்துவகாரிய கிரியா சோதி ஐக்கிய லக்ஷிய காளாமுகசைவ முத்தி உலகு.
20. வயிந்துவகாரிய பிரணவாகார லக்ஷிய கணாதிபத்தியசைவ முத்தி உலகு.
21. வயிந்துவகாரிய சத்துவாகார லக்ஷிய ஸ்தானாதிபத்திய சைவ முத்தி உலகு.
22. வயிந்துவகாரிய தாமச சத்துவாகார லக்ஷிய பத்திரசைவ முத்தி உலகு.
translation: 1. The world of the Agama Suddha Saiva liberation, whose aim is the gross action of outward worship, in the contemplation of the self as Sadasiva, toward the Sadakhya with form and formless, foremost of the five, born of the conjunction of what has form and what is formless.

2. The world of the Kriya-jnana Suddha Saiva liberation, whose aim is the action, in notion, of inward worship, in the contemplation of the self as Sadasiva, toward the Sadakhya with form and formless, foremost of the five, born of the conjunction of what has form and what is formless.
3. The world of the Asuddha Saiva liberation, whose aim is the deficient action of worship of the form, with distinctions, on the three grounds, a part of the tattvas.

4. The world of the Misra Saiva liberation, whose aim is devotion (upasana) that holds the Veda and the Agama equal, with the contemplation of non-duality in relation to the five acts in general and the contemplation of non-duality in relation to the five acts in particular.

5. The world of the Siddhanta Saiva liberation, dualist in the pure tattvas Shakti and Siva, with distinctions, arising from pure Bindu, with the certainty of the self as distinct from the effects of maya.

6. The world of the Anadi Saiva liberation, whose aim is the Brahman of the five pranavas, the limbs of knowledge produced from Bindu at the end of the four Shaktis, the partial cause of the universe of word and meaning.

7. The world of the Avantara Saiva liberation, with the certainty of the worship of the five agents, whose five aims are the centres at the end of the navel, the end of the throat, the end of the forehead, the end of the brahmarandhra and the dvadasanta.

8. The world of the Bheda Saiva liberation, whose aim is the worship of Sadakhya as agent, arising from Bindu, with the certainty of the pure self through the subduing of karma with distinctions and of the six paths by nirvana initiation (diksha).

9. The world of the Anu Saiva liberation, which does not accept the Sadakhya with distinctions, with form and with form and formless, arising from Bindu, and accepts the formless of Bindu with distinctions.

10. The world of the Adi Saiva liberation, with the certainty of the own form of the linga in all universes, bodies and pedestals produced from Bindu with distinctions, and in all souls with impurity.
11. The world of the Pasupata Saiva liberation, whose aim is the experience of knowledge in Bindu, pure maya, with the conclusion that the self, whose own form is knowledge, attains lordship.
12. The world of the Vamatantra Saiva liberation, whose aim is the distinction of consciousness alone, the effects of maya in the form of the six paths being superimposed on it.
13. The world of the Vama-advaita Saiva liberation, whose aim is the excellence of consciousness alone as the ground, free of the effects of maya in the form of the six paths.

14. The world of the dualist Vama Saiva liberation, with the doctrine that the soul's light, its power of consciousness released from impurity, is equal to the own power of consciousness that is not other than Siva.
15. The world of the Misra Vama Saiva liberation, whose aim is the power of the great maya, the material cause of the bodies, instruments and knowledge of all own forms beginning with Nada.
16. The world of the Vama Siddhanta liberation, whose aim is full oneness in the light that takes hold of the general arising of the power with all differences and distinctions.
17. The world of the Bhairava Saiva liberation, whose aim is the manifold distinctions aided by Bindu.
18. The world of the Kalamukha Saiva liberation, whose aim is oneness with the light of action produced from Bindu, through the vow of Siva.
19. The world of the Mahavrata Saiva liberation, the experience of oneness in the conjunction of the limb and the linga.
20. The world of the Ganadhipatya Saiva liberation, whose aim is the form of the pranava produced from Bindu.
21. The world of the Sthanadhipatya Saiva liberation, whose aim is the form of sattva produced from Bindu.
22. The world of the Bhadra Saiva liberation, whose aim is the tamasic and sattvic form produced from Bindu.
23. The world of the Mantra Saiva liberation, whose aim is what is produced from Bindu.
24. The world of the Yantra Saiva liberation, aided by Bindu.
25. The world of the Karma Saiva liberation, whose aim is prarabdha (the karma already bearing fruit), produced from maya.
commentary: Twenty-five Saiva schools, each with the liberation it holds and the aim it sets: outward worship, inward worship, non-duality, lordship, the linga, oneness with light, and so on. Vallalar counts each as a world of means and attainment in the pure tattvas. He names what each aims at and where that aim comes from: most are "produced from Bindu", some from maya.

translation: 1. The world of the Vaidika Saiva Siddhanta liberation of the instrumental and material cause alone, whose aim is the experience of the own form contained within subtle notion.
2. The world of the Vijnana Vaidika Siddhanta liberation, whose aim is the experience of pure consciousness alone.
3. The world of the inward Vaidika Saiva Siddhanta liberation, whose aim is the experience of the separate self.
4. The world of the outward and inward Vaidika Saiva Siddhanta liberation, the experience of the oneness of the supreme and the soul.
5. The world of the strong non-dualist Vaidika Saiva Siddhanta liberation, whose aim is the experience of the oneness of the separate self with Siva.
6. The world of the Vaidika Saiva Siddhanta liberation, the experience of the three states of the individual soul.
7. The world of the Vaidika Saiva Siddhanta liberation, the experience of the three states of Isvara.

8. The world of the Vaidika Saiva Siddhanta liberation of the experience of the supreme turiya in Siva-waking, the experience of swallowing the universe in Siva-dreaming, and the experience of utter stillness in Siva-deep-sleep.
1. The world of the Isvara-aikya Saiva Siddhanta liberation, whose aim is the experience of the oneness of the soul and the supreme, through the balance of body and karma.
2. The world of the Prajnabhanga Saiva Siddhanta liberation, whose aim is a swoon in which the soul's own knowing is destroyed, the soul's light of consciousness without distinctions.
3. The world of the Bheda Saiva Siddhanta liberation, whose aim is the cessation of impurity with the soul in duality, through the analogy of the tarnish of copper and the pill.
4. The world of the Sivasamavada Saiva Siddhanta liberation, whose aim is the experience of equality with Siva, through the analogy of the wasp and the worm.
5. The world of the Sankranta Saiva Siddhanta liberation, whose aim is the experience of Sivahood with Siva's instruments, through the subduing of the beginningless impurity.

6. The world of the Isvara-avikara Saiva Siddhanta liberation, whose aim is the experience of the oneness of the soul as shadow with the Lord's feet, through the analogy of the tree, the body and the shadow.

7. The world of the Nimittakarana-parinama Saiva Siddhanta liberation, whose aim is the experience of the own form, the light of consciousness not other than all: the tattvas, the tattvic, the kinds of maya and the kinds of souls.
8. The world of the Anupaksha Siddhanta liberation.
9. The world of the Sambhupaksha Siddhanta liberation.
10. The world of the Siddhanta liberation of the oneness of Siva and the supreme.
commentary: Eight Vaidika Saiva Siddhanta liberations and ten of the Saiva Siddhanta schools follow, each named by the experience it holds as liberation. Several are known by their images. Copper loses its tarnish through the alchemist's pill, as the soul loses its impurity. The worm becomes like the wasp that stings it, as the soul becomes like Siva. The soul joins the Lord's feet like a shadow. These too are worlds of means and attainment in the pure tattvas.

commentary: The five states of the soul (avattai), waking, dreaming, deep sleep, turiya (the fourth) and the transcendent, are counted in each of three conditions, in liberation and in bondage. In the sakala condition the soul is joined to body and instruments; in the kevala it lies alone with its darkness (anava); in the pure condition it is freed by grace. Liberation and bondage are then counted in the causal form of each condition.

2. The world of the particular power of consciousness, as the cause of knowledge, the particular limb of the causal awareness of inherence in Siva, effected through the joy of consciousness in knowledge alone in the pure, subtle soul.

3. The world of the particular power of consciousness, as the cause of action, the particular limb of the causal awareness of inherence in Siva, effected through the joy of consciousness in action alone in the pure, subtle soul.

1. The world of the particular supreme Power, as the cause of desire, the particular limb of the causal awareness of inherence in Siva, effected through the fullness of joy in desire alone in the pure, subtle soul.

2. The world of the particular supreme Power, as the cause of knowledge, the particular limb of the causal awareness of inherence in Siva, effected through the fullness of joy in knowledge alone in the pure, subtle soul.

commentary: The group closes with the soul's own powers in their pure, subtle form: desire, knowledge, action, consciousness and the supreme Power. Each is taken in turn as the cause of the five, so that twenty-five worlds result. All are limbs of one awareness: the soul knowing its inherence in Siva. Here practice gives way to the soul's own powers, purified and turned toward Siva, and its joy begins.

translation: (5. The worlds beyond the causal)
Now the worlds beyond the causal:

1. The world of the power of direct perception reaching through before and after, over the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the elements, in the gross, general experience of charya-charya in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

2. The world of the power of direct perception of the non-conscious, over the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the elements, in the gross, general experience of charya-kriya in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

3. The world of the power of relinquishing the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the elements, in the state of the gross, general experience of charya-yoga in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

1. The world of the power of direct perception reaching through before and after, over the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the senses, in the state of the gross, general experience of charya-jnana in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

2. The world of the power of direct perception of the non-conscious, over the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the senses, in the state of the gross, general experience of kriya-charya in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

3. The world of the power of relinquishing the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the senses, in the state of the gross, general experience of kriya-kriya in the outer-outer of pure awareness.
In the same way:
Count also the organs of knowledge and their objects, and the organs of action and their objects.

1. The world of the power of direct perception reaching through before and after, over the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the instruments, in the state of the gross, general experience of kriya-yoga in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

2. The world of the power of direct perception of the non-conscious, over the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the instruments, in the state of the gross, general experience of kriya-jnana in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

3. The world of the power of relinquishing the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the instruments, in the state of the gross and subtle, general experience of yoga-charya in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

1. The world of the power of direct perception reaching through before and after, over the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of prakriti of the three gunas, in the state of the subtle, general experience of yoga-kriya in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

2. The world of the power of direct perception of the non-conscious, over the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of prakriti of the three gunas, in the state of the subtle, general experience of yoga-yoga in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

3. The world of the power of relinquishing the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of prakriti of the three gunas, in the subtle, general experience of yoga-jnana in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

1. The world of the power of direct perception reaching through before and after, over the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the pure-impure tattvas beginning with kalā, in the subtle, particular experience of jnana-charya in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

2. The world of the power of direct perception of the non-conscious, over the form, own form, nature, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the pure-impure tattvas beginning with kalā, in the subtle, particular experience of jnana-kriya in the outer-outer of pure awareness.

3. The world of the power of relinquishing the form, own form, pervaded, pervading, particular, quality and the rest of the pure-impure tattvas beginning with kalā, in the subtle, particular experience of jnana-yoga in the outer-outer of pure awareness.
commentary: The fifth group goes beyond every cause. Each tattva is now met three times: in the power of direct perception that sees it through, before and after, from its origin to its end; in the power that perceives it as non-conscious (acittu), not the self; and in the power that relinquishes it. This matches the Saiva steps of seeing the tattvas, knowing them as inert, and leaving them behind. The ladder starts from the elements, and each rung is held in pure awareness (cutta camvētam) and in one of the sixteen stages of the four ways.

commentary: The ascent continues through the pure tattvas, pure vidya, Mahesvara and Sadakhya, and then through the paths (adhvas) by which all worlds are ordered: bhuvana, mantra, word, letter and kalā. It rises to speech born of Nada, Nada born of Bindu, and Bindu itself. Each is seen through, known as non-conscious, and relinquished. The sixteen stages of the four ways run in order through the outer-outer and the outer of pure awareness, and begin again in the inner-outer.

commentary: In the inner of pure awareness the lower desire, knowledge and action are seen through and left, and then the lower Bindu and Nada, so that the four cycles of the sixteen stages are complete. Next come the bonds themselves: karma, the inborn impurity (anava), Tirodhai the veiling power, Kudilai (pure maya stirring as Om), and the causal states of the soul. Even these are perceived for what they are and relinquished. In 353 only the changed words are printed; the subject of item 1 carries over.

commentary: In the inner-inner of pure awareness the soul meets the supreme Powers, itself, and the supreme Siva. The middle power changes here: no longer perceiving something as non-conscious, it perceives consciousness, partially for the supreme desire, action and the soul, and completely for the supreme Power. For the supreme Siva it is the complete perception of Being. What is let go is now only latent impressions (vācaṉā), the last traces of past experience. Even the supreme Nada is relinquished.

sections.title: The Worlds Beyond the Causal: The Final Experiences, and the Close

tamil: 1. பிரத்தியேக ரூபப் பிரத்தியக்ஷ ஞான ஆன்மானுபவ உலகு.

11. ஞானயோக போகாதீத சொரூப சாக்ஷாத்கார வியாபக வியாப்பியானுபவ சாக்கிராதீத சுத்தாவத்தை உலகு.
